blocks.content: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad (AMD)

Ever dreamed of stepping into a living history book? In the heart of Gujarat lies one such city soaked in history and heritage. Located in the district of Mehsana, Vadnagar isn't just another old city but your gateway to experiencing centuries of fascinating Indian history firsthand.

As you wander its winding lanes, you'll walk the same paths once graced by mighty empires like the Mauryas, Guptas, Chavdas, and Solankis. Today, you can lose yourself in Vadnagar's maze-like streets, where every corner surprises you. Ancient temples stand proud, telling tales of devotion. Robust fortifications whisper secrets of past glory. And the best part? This place lets you experience Gujarat's golden past at your own pace.
Come and explore this historic city, which has witnessed the passage of centuries and the rise and fall of dynasties.

Begin your Vadnagar expedition with its crown jewel – the magnificent Kirti Torans, two towering gateways that have watched over the city for around 900 years. These twin arches stand by the peaceful Sharmistha Lake; look closely at these 12th-century masterpieces and see a world of art carved into stone. Every inch reveals something new, from graceful animals, dancing figures, and divine beings to nature's beauty, captured in lotus flowers and twisting vines.

Visit at sunrise for a truly special moment when the morning light streams through these grand arches. It's the same view that travellers, traders, and royalty have enjoyed for centuries – and now it's yours to discover.

Continue your journey through time at the Vadnagar Museum , a treasure house that brings the city's rich past to life. Housed in a colonial-era building, this museum showcases rare artefacts discovered during excavations. After learning about Vadnagar’s heritage, if you want to see its spiritual side, head to the Hatkeshwar Temple, a spiritual landmark that has drawn devotees for years. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, this architectural marvel showcases the signature Solanki style with ornate pillars and detailed stone carvings. The temple's peaceful courtyard offers you a perfect spot for quiet contemplation. Local devotees believe the temple's Shiva lingam appeared naturally, making it even more special for worshippers who flock here during festivals like Mahashivratri.

Speaking of festivities, Vadnagar celebrates the Tana Riri Festival, a musical tribute to two remarkable sisters with healing voices. The story goes back to Mughal Emperor Akbar's time when his celebrated court musician Tansen's health began to fail. Enter Tana and Riri, two gifted sisters from Vadnagar, who came to his rescue by performing Raag Malhar, cooling his fever through the power of their music.

Today, the festival transforms Vadnagar into a celebration of India's rich musical heritage. Musicians from around the country gather here to create magical evenings filled with soul-stirring melodies. The festival's highlight is the prestigious Tana Riri Award, presented to outstanding musicians.
To experience the same musical magic that once flowed through Vadnagar's ancient streets, plan your trip in November.

Although Vadnagar is a treat to the soul at any given point of the year, you can plan your visit during the cooler days, typically from October to March. The charming little town dipped in history and divine energy will welcome you with open arms and give you a wholesome life experience.
